claude_take: AI keeps cutting both ways at once: Anthropic made agentic coding dramatically cheaper the same week OpenAI's Astra crossed into the cybersecurity capability the field has been dreading, and X's brand-new payments feature is already drawing mass account-takeover attempts. California's legislature worked past a midnight deadline to protect its film-tax-credit dollars, proof the money moves fast when it wants to, while Maggie Gyllenhaal had to say out loud that financing for women directors still doesn't move at all. A 40,000-student study landed on the same shape from a different angle: kids reaching for AI chatbots because the humans around them aren't reaching back. The money moves fast; the people don't.
claude_take_title: The Money Moves Fast; the People Don't

items.headline: Anthropic Launches Claude Fable 5.1 and Mythos 5.1, Cutting Agentic Coding Costs by Up to 45%
items.summary: Anthropic introduced Claude Fable 5.1 and Claude Mythos 5.1, the same underlying model released with different levels of safeguards: Fable 5.1 is generally available, while Mythos 5.1 is restricted to trusted-access programs. The new model matches or beats Fable 5 at low and medium effort and jumps sharply at higher effort tiers, more than doubling Fable 5's Terminal-Bench-Science score and leading CursorBench's agentic-coding benchmark. Base pricing is unchanged, but a cut to cache-read costs lowers typical workload costs by about 25 percent and highly agentic work by up to 45 percent, and Anthropic says Claude Code users should see roughly 60 percent fewer cybersecurity false positives.

items.headline: OpenAI Says Astra Is First Model to Cross 'Critical' Cybersecurity Threshold
items.summary: OpenAI said its upcoming Astra model is the first to exceed the "Critical" tier of its Preparedness Framework for cybersecurity, scoring a perfect result on the ExploitBench benchmark and autonomously discovering two previously unknown zero-day vulnerabilities during testing without step-by-step human guidance. Crossing that threshold triggers stricter internal safeguards under OpenAI's own framework, and the company says it will restrict Astra's most powerful cyber capabilities to vetted defenders when the model becomes available. It is a milestone researchers have warned about for years: an AI system that can independently find and exploit security flaws in hardened real-world systems, a capability that cuts both ways for attackers and defenders alike.

items.headline: Venice Jury President Maggie Gyllenhaal Calls Lack of Female Directors 'A Systemic Problem'
items.summary: At the opening press conference of the 83rd Venice Film Festival, jury president Maggie Gyllenhaal directly challenged this year's competition lineup, which includes just one film directed by a woman, down from six a year earlier. She said the imbalance reflects a systemic financing problem rather than a talent gap, and questioned whether the stories women choose to tell are simply undervalued as "high art." Her remarks came at a festival that only added a female-codirected Gaza documentary to its lineup last week after criticism, putting fresh pressure on Venice and the wider industry over who actually gets funded to direct.

items.headline: California Legislature Passes Film Tax Credit Cap Exemptions, Heads to Newsom's Desk
items.summary: California lawmakers passed SB 186 just before their legislative session's midnight deadline, fully exempting independent-film tax credits from a new statewide cap that otherwise limits corporations to offsetting $5 million in tax liability a year. The bill, a final step after studios and legislators struck a compromise days earlier, also lets productions redeem credits for cash in two years instead of five and extends the window to use older non-refundable credits from nine years to fifteen. Governor Gavin Newsom is expected to sign it, protecting the state's $750 million production incentive program that the industry warned the new corporate tax cap would otherwise undercut.

items.headline: Attackers Target X Accounts With Mass Password-Reset Emails After X Money Launch
items.summary: X says attackers are mass-triggering its public password-reset form, flooding users with unsolicited emails, some receiving up to ten in a matter of hours, in an apparent attempt to gain access to accounts around the rollout of X Money, the platform's new bank-card-linked payments service for creators. X engineering says it has found no evidence of a successful breach and is investigating, while the company's general counsel vowed to pursue those responsible. The episode underscores the stakes of turning a social platform into a financial one: attackers already have years of leaked credentials to draw on, and a payments feature gives them a much sharper reason to use them.

items.headline: Study of Nearly 40,000 Students Links Using AI Chatbots for Emotional Support to Higher Loneliness
items.summary: A University of Ottawa study of 39,761 Ontario students in grades 4 through 12 found that the roughly 21 percent who turned to AI chatbots for emotional support or relationship advice were significantly more likely to report clinical-level emotional difficulties, loneliness, and a diminished sense of mattering to others, even after accounting for demographics and existing loneliness. The tendency was higher among older students and among racialized and gender-diverse youth. Researchers stressed that chatbot use likely isn't causing the distress so much as signaling it: a marker that a young person needs more real human connection and support, not less.

items.headline: Moschino Names Ex-Sunnei Duo Loris Messina and Simone Rizzo Co-Creative Directors
items.summary: Moschino appointed Loris Messina and Simone Rizzo as co-creative directors effective immediately, succeeding Adrian Appiolaza after his two-year run at the house. The pair founded and ran the independent label Sunnei, known for witty, crowd-participatory runway shows, since 2014, and will make their Moschino debut at Milan Fashion Week this month. It's a bet that Moschino's original irreverence is better rebuilt by designers who built their own brand on humor and irony than by a single star name.

items.headline: Cardiff Study Links Irritability and Anxiety in ADHD to Higher Depression Risk
items.summary: Researchers at Cardiff University's Wolfson Centre for Young People's Mental Health, led by Dr. Lucy Riglin, found that irritability and anxiety in childhood and young adulthood, and negative thought patterns in adolescence, largely explain why people with ADHD face a higher risk of later depression. The findings point to a concrete prevention target: screening for these emotional and cognitive patterns in children and young people with ADHD, rather than waiting for depression to appear, could help catch and treat it earlier. The study also found sex differences the researchers link to girls and women with ADHD typically being diagnosed later, which delays support.

items.headline: Foucault's Panopticon
items.summary: Michel Foucault used Jeremy Bentham's Panopticon, a prison design where a single guard in a central tower can potentially see every inmate at once, as a model for how modern power actually works: not through constant force, but through the possibility of being watched. Because inmates never know exactly when they are observed, they discipline themselves as if they always are, and that self-monitoring is cheaper and more thorough than any guard could be. Foucault argued this same logic, hierarchical observation, normalizing judgment, and examination, quietly organizes schools, hospitals, workplaces, and militaries, training people to police their own behavior long before an authority ever has to intervene. It remains one of the sharpest lenses for thinking about surveillance, from CCTV to today's always-on digital platforms.
